simple.meaning: עָרַךְ (ʻârak) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to set in a row , i.e. arrange , put in order (in a very wide variety of applications).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 76 times across Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Joshua, and 14 more, beginning at Genesis 14:8. Its contexts include family line, altar, covenant, kingship, priesthood, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָרַךְ (H6186).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: עָרַךְ (ʻârak) / H6186 is traced through Genesis 14:8, Genesis 22:9, Exodus 27:21, Exodus 40:4 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: to set in a row , i.e. arrange , put in order (in a very wide variety of applications)
definitions.usage: put (set) (the battle, self) in array, compare, direct, equal, esteem, estimate, expert (in war), furnish, handle, join (battle), ordain, (lay, put, reckon up, set) (in) order, prepare, tax, value.
